questions.question:
Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain a grammatical error. Select the option that has the error. If there is no error, select ‘No error’.

Rohit Sharma’s century was very acclaimed in the media.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase 'very acclaimed' is incorrect. The correct phrase should be 'highly acclaimed'.
 
• The word **'acclaimed'** is often paired with **'highly'** to indicate a significant level of praise.
 
 
• Example: *Her performance was **highly acclaimed** by critics.*
 
• *Example : She even found time to record a handful of **highly acclaimed** albums.*
 
 

Hence, the correct statement is ***Rohit Sharma's century was highly acclaimed__ in the media.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• When using adjectives to describe the extent of praise or criticism, it's important to use the** correct intensifier**.

 
 
• **Example:** *His efforts were **greatly appreciated** by the team.*
 
 
 
• Commonly used **intensifiers** with adjectives include **'highly', 'greatly', 'deeply',** etc., depending on the context.
 
 
• **Example:** *The movie was** deeply moving** and left a lasting impression.*

questions.question:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Had you been / working regularly, / you had completed / the project yesterday.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"had"** is used as the past tense of 'have' to indicate possession or a past action. However, in conditional sentences, it is paired with the past perfect form.

 
 
• **Example: **They** had **finished the work before the deadline.
 
 
 
• **"would have"** is used in the past conditional tense to indicate an action that would have happened if a certain condition had been met. (होगा)
 
 
• **Example: **If you had called me, I **would have** come.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct phrase should be "you would have completed" instead of "you had completed".

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Had you been** (क्या तुम होते): This phrase is correctly used in the past perfect continuous tense.

 
 
• **Example:** Had you been more careful, the accident would have been avoided.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: the project yesterday** (प्रोजेक्ट कल): This phrase correctly indicates the timing of the project completion.
 
 
• **Example:** I submitted the project yesterday.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: working regularly** (नियमित रूप से काम कर रहे): This phrase correctly shows the continuous action.
 
 
• **Example:** She has been working regularly on her fitness goals.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

It is a cheap reasonably / restaurant in this part of the town / where you can eat / delicious food.

options.text: restaurant in this part of the town

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the third part of the given sentence, the order of adjectives is incorrect.
 
• The correct order should be: **opinion + size + age + shape + color + origin + material + purpose**.
 
• In the given sentence, **reasonably** is an **adverb** and **cheap** is an** adjective.**
 
• Therefore, the correct order should be "reasonably cheap" instead of "cheap reasonably".

 

Hence, the correct statement is: ***It is a reasonably cheap __restaurant in this part of the town where you can eat delicious food*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The **order of adjectives **is crucial for the sentence to make sense and sound natural.
 
• **Adverbs usually modify adjectives, verbs, or other adverbs,** and should be placed in the correct order to maintain the intended meaning of the sentence.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that has a grammatical error.

I am working with him since 2002, / but even today / I am unable / to understand his motives.

options.text: I am working with him since 2002,

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the present perfect continuous tense should be used instead of the present continuous tense.
 
• Since the action of working with him started in the past (in 2002) and continues to the present, the correct tense is **present perfect continuous**.
 
• The correct form should be **"*I have been working with him since 2002*."**

Hence, the correct statement is** "*I have been working with him since 2002__, but even today I am unable to understand his motives."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The present perfect continuous tense is used to show that something started in the past and has continued up until now.
 
• It is formed with **"have/has been" + present participle (verb + ing).**
 
• **Example:** ***She has been reading for two hours.***

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

He are very thirsty. / Give him / a little water to drink.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is: '**He are very thirsty'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **error** in the given sentence is the use of **'are'** after the singular pronoun **'He'.**
 
• Here, the subject is a **singular** third-person pronoun **'He'**, so the corresponding verb form should also be singular **'is'**.
 
 
• **Corrected sentence:** *"He is very thirsty. / Give him / a little water to drink."*
 
 
 
• This maintains the proper subject-verb agreement, and the sentence is grammatically correct.
 
• Hence, **'He are very thirsty'** is the erroneous part.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• According to subject-verb agreement, when the subject is a singular third-person pronoun like '**he',** '**she'** or '**it'** the corresponding verb form should also be singular.

 
 
• **Incorrect:** *She are going to the market.*
 
• **Correct:** *She is going to the market.*

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that has a grammatical error.

When he resigned, / the company offered him / a huge sum of money but / he refused to agree to it.

options.text: a huge sum of money but
he refused to agree to it.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is ** Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the third part of the given sentence, the phrase 'refused to agree to it' is redundant.
 
• In the given sentence, the verb **'refused'** already implies **not agreeing**. So the correct word should be '**he refused'.**
 
• Therefore, the phrase **'refused to agree to it'** should be **revised** to avoid **redundancy.**
 
 
• **Example:** ***He refused the offer*.**
 
 

Hence, the correct statement is **"*When he resigned, the company offered him a huge sum of money but he refused."__***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• If the **sentence contains redundant phrases** that **repeat the same idea**, it is **best to revise** the sentence for clarity.

 
 
• **Example:** *The manager **approved** the proposal **and gave his consent**.* (This can be revised to *The manager approved the proposal*.)
 
 
 
• Always aim for **conciseness** in writing to make your point **clear and effective**.
 
 
• Example: *She **returned back** the book.* (This can be revised to *She returned the book*.)

questions.question:

questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.**

Raman ate the cake and exclaimed that it tasted sweetly.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **it tasted sweetly**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The word **"sweetly"** is an **adverb**. However, in this context, the word should describe the taste of the cake, not the manner in which the taste is perceived.
 
• The appropriate word here should be **"sweet,"** which is an **adjective** that describes the characteristic of the taste.
 
• When referring to the **senses **(taste, smell, look, feel, sound), **adjectives **are used rather than **adverbs**.
 
• For example, "tastes sweet," "smells good," "looks beautiful."
 
• Using "sweetly" can lead to confusion, as it implies how something is tasted rather than the characteristic of the taste itself.

Therefore, the correct answer is- **it tasted sweet**.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that has a grammatical error.

Soldiers in / the Indian Armed Forces are / trained never to / fight cowardice.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The word **"cowardly"** means lacking courage; it is an adverb describing an action done without bravery or courage. (कायरतापूर्ण)

 
 
• **Example: **He acted **cowardly** by running away from his responsibilities.
 
 
 
• **"Cowardice"** is the noun form and refers to the lack of bravery. (कायरता)
 
 
• **Example: **His** cowardice **was evident when he refused to stand up for his friend.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the correct word should be** "cowardly" **used as an adverb to describe how the soldiers should never fight.
 
• "Cowardly" is indeed an adjective, but the correct structure requires "in a cowardly manner" to form an adverbial phrase that modifies the verb "fight."

**Therefore, the correct sentence is:** Soldiers in the Indian Armed Forces are trained never to fight in a cowardly manner**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

• **Example:** Soldiers in the army are trained to handle various combat situations.
 
 
 
• **the Indian Armed Forces are** (भारतीय सशस्त्र बल): Refers to the combined military forces of India, including the Army, Navy, and Air Force.
 
 
• **Example: **The Indian Armed Forces are known for their discipline and valor.
 
 
 
• **trained never to** (प्रशिक्षित): Refers to the rigorous training soldiers undergo to prepare for various situations.
 
 
• **Example:** Soldiers are trained never to leave a comrade behind.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

Health insurance __are important__ today since anyone can face a medical emergency without warning.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence is:** is important.**
 
• The sentence is **discussing the importance of health insurance in the present time. **Therefore, **the verb tense needs** to be in** the present tense** to indicate current relevance.** **
 
• **"Is" is the present tense form of the verb "to be," **and it correctly indicates the ongoing importance of health insurance in the present.
 
• ***The correct sentence would be:**__ "Health insurance is important today since anyone can face a medical emergency without warning."*
 
• **Options 1, 2, and 3** (**"will be important," "has been important," and "was important"**) are incorrect because they use verb tenses that are not suitable for indicating present relevance.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

We were driving home when suddenly a deer runs across the road.

options.text: a deer runs across the road

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the third part of the given sentence, the present tense 'runs' is incorrect.
 
• The sentence describes an action that was ongoing in the past when another event occurred suddenly.
 
• Therefore, the verb 'runs' should be in the past tense to match the context of the sentence.
 
• Hence, the correct form of the verb 'runs' should be 'ran'.

Hence, the correct statement is **'*We were driving home when suddenly a deer ran across the road__*__.__**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• When describing past events, it is important to maintain consistency in the verb tenses.
 
• In this case, the ongoing action (**'were driving**') sets the scene in the past, and the sudden event **('ran across')** should also be in the past tense.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

As is usual with stories of this genre, / in spite of their varying socio political realities, / the youngsters have fallen in love / with each other madly.

options.text: the youngsters have fallen in love
in spite of their varying socio political realities
As is usual with stories of this genre

questions.solution:
The correct answer is As is usual with stories of this genre.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence that contains the error is 'As is usual with stories of this genre'.
 
• As is a conjunction and an adverb and is used before a clause, another adverb or a clause beginning with a preposition.
 
 
• *Example: She enjoys all kinds of music, as I do.*
 
 
 
• Therefore the use of 'as is usual' in the sentence should be replaced with 'as usual' to make it grammatically correct.

​

*Correct sentence: As usual with stories of this genre in spite of their varying socio political realities, the youngsters have fallen in love with each other madly.*

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

There is a spectrum / of seas around that / land which attracts / tourists of all aging.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1. **"tourists of all aging".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The phrase **"tourists of all aging"** is incorrect in this context. The issue here is with the word "**aging**."
 
• The **correct **phrase should be **"tourists of all ages."**
 
• "Ages" refers to people of all age groups, while "aging" is a process of becoming older, which does not fit logically in this sentence.
 
• Replacing "aging" with "ages" corrects the grammatical error and makes the sentence meaningful.

Therefore, the correct answer is- *There is a spectrum of seas around that land which attracts tourists of all ages.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2 ("There is a spectrum"): This part of the sentence is correctly framed. It correctly introduces the idea that there is a range or variety present, in this case, referring to seas.
 
• Option 3 ("land which attracts"): This segment is correctly constructed as well. It indicates that the land attracts something, which is a proper use of attraction in a sentence.
 
• Option 4 ("of seas around that"): This phrase correctly provides additional information about the spectrum mentioned in Option 2, indicating the variety of seas surrounding a specific area.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

The innocent clerk was accused with misappropriating funds of the company.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the phrase 'was accused with' is incorrect. The correct phrase should be **'was accused of'.**
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase 'was accused of' should be used in place of the incorrect phrase 'was accused with'.
 
 
• ***Babita is accused of __stealing the money***
 
 

Hence, the correct statement is '***The innocent clerk was__ accused of __misappropriating funds of the company*.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• When using the verb 'accuse', it is always followed by the preposition 'of' to indicate the reason for the accusation.
 
 
• **Example:** *She was** accused of **theft*.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Himalayas include the highest mountains in the world and feed almost 20% of the earth’s population.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**)

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the omission of the article "**the**" before "**Himalayas**."
 
• Proper nouns that refer to mountain ranges, rivers, and some other geographical features typically require the definite article "the" before them.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**The Himalayas include**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 4** of the sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

**Correct Sentence:** *"**The Himalayas include** the highest mountains in the world and feed almost 20% of the earth's population."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "almost 20% of the earth's population."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 2: "highest mountains in"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 3: "the world and feed"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
